A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FLoC study. All 21 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable. Retained equations, tables and illustrations can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark accuracies, compression timings, block-length experiments, token-distribution analyses and qualitative examples in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds EgoSchema evaluations, additional baseline comparisons, resource profiling and a similarity-metric ablation.

M1.justification: The facility-location objective, cosine-similarity default, temporal blocking and lazy-greedy Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. V2 expands the algorithm explanation and tests a Gaussian Euclidean alternative in an ablation, without changing the proposed default procedure.

E1.justification: Section 4.2 and Table 1 add EgoSchema, extending evaluation to minute-level egocentric clips emphasizing schema-level reasoning and activity prediction. Video-MME, MLVU, LongVideoBench and the extended-video scenario remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 1 add STTM, LLaVA Scissor and FastVID, substantially expanding the primary comparator suite. STTM and Scissor are evaluated with both main backbones; FastVID is evaluated only with Qwen2.5-VL. The clustering baselines already present in v1 are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds a resource-evaluation protocol measuring inference/compression/total time, FLOPs and peak VRAM on Qwen2.5-VL-7B/H100 with 784 frames, 60 tokens per frame and 12.5% retention. It also adds controlled similarity comparisons and T=128 to the block-length sweep. Table 1 averages four benchmarks instead of three; existing main compression ratios and extended-video settings remain.

E4.justification: The block-length analysis expands from Video-MME in v1 Table 4 to three datasets in v2 Figure 6. New Appendix H tests cosine versus Gaussian Euclidean similarity, while Appendix G examines computational and memory costs. Earlier representativeness, task-specific and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Appendix A retains the same 50-video sample and per-video standardization; that normalization is not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds EgoSchema, new-baseline, profiling, similarity-ablation and expanded block-length results. Table 8 reports Euclidean-minus-cosine average differences of +0.55, -0.27 and -0.97 across the three retention ratios. Matched original benchmark scores remain unchanged, but Table 2 changes the 7B baseline average from 65.72 to 65.82 and the stated gain from 1.31 to 1.21 despite unchanged component scores. Table 1 averages now cover four benchmarks.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds the formal diminishing-returns inequality and an argument explaining why stale marginal gains provide upper bounds for lazy-greedy selection. Appendix H defines the Gaussian Euclidean similarity used in its ablation. The original objective and approximation guarantee remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contribution: training-free, model-agnostic, query-agnostic facility-location compression with efficient, representative token selection. EgoSchema and additional comparisons provide new support without substantively redefining that contribution.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving graph merging's weak connections, cosine similarity's advantages under strong compression, and pairwise similarities' FLOP costs. Section 4.5.3 changes the large-block interpretation from substantial computational overhead to negligible latency and a robust fixed default, although the retained limitations in Appendix I still describe an overhead tradeoff.

D1.justification: Appendix E adds implementation sources, default-setting and threshold-adjustment information for the new baselines. Appendices G–H document the profiling workload, operation-count estimation, PyTorch memory measurement and Gaussian bandwidth heuristic. Conversely, Table 1 removes absolute token-count columns, reducing explicit budget documentation.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations for STTM, LLaVA Scissor, FastVID and EgoSchema, and contrasts FLoC with graph-based merging through the weak-connection discussion. The related-work taxonomy and foundational positioning around facility location and submodular optimization remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract and citation formatting, condenses benchmark descriptions, expands the lazy-greedy explanation and rewrites portions of the results discussion. It inserts Appendices G–H, moves limitations to Appendix I, and updates affiliations and publication headers. Most narrative and section ordering remain.

P2.justification: Table 1 is expanded and restructured, and Table 2 changes from stacked to side-by-side model comparisons. Figure 1 is redrawn with additional comparators; the block-length table becomes a three-panel plot. Profiling and similarity tables are added. Earlier appendix scatter plots, qualitative examples and t-SNE illustrations are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: Additional comparator coverage and controlled similarity/block-length analyses strengthen the evidence for FLoC's effectiveness and design choices. The net gain is limited by reporting regressions: Table 2's revised baseline average disagrees with its component scores, Table 7 reports full-token total time below inference time, and the negligible-latency interpretation conflicts with retained timing evidence and limitations.
